faithful: the Predictor / Constructor / Scheduler three-part structure
the predictor separates run latency, peak memory and model-loading cost
prediction-conditioned scheduling rather than reading execution truth
same-deployment linear-chain fusion, one grant and one load serving a fused chain
predicted release and completion drive scheduling
ready work first, with fusion competing through completion improvement
adapted: a train-only tabular request-conditioned predictor replaces the graph-encoder predictor
min_support=3 as a frozen adaptation hyperparameter
lane as the device-context proxy in this simulator
predictor targets map to compute / load / total peak
Eq.12 maps to a single-commit scheduler
replica and deployment lifecycle map to the unified GPU residency/prefetch abstraction
deviation: the paper's operator data-flow graph encoder, full device feature vector and sequence-length/output-bucket predictor are not reproduced
there is no full model-replica / serving-queue / batch-server abstraction
scale-out and the full reclaim-victim / distant-next-use lifecycle policy are not reproduced; reclaim still follows the substrate admission mechanism
KV and prefix-cache serving mechanisms are not reproduced
no full multi-step physical-plan optimisation; a rolling single-commit adaptation in the current simulator instead

non_degeneracy_evidence.interpretation: every request uses the finest tier, so min_support=3 has not degenerated the predictions to (model, lane)

defects_closed_before_freeze: predicted_duration_ms read node.compute_ms, the node's actual intrinsic compute time
the Eq.12 key carried an invented -boundaries_removed tie-break
the truth fallback was blocked only at the simulator wrapper, so the scheduler's own entry points still read node.workspace_peak_mb
the non-degeneracy gate compared tables[1] directly, bypassing min_support and the production backoff
runtime and total-peak were decomposed inconsistently with the substrate, double-counting the load and inflating the admission peak
freeze_breaking_exception: A reproducible correctness bug with freeze-breaking provenance; the tiers, support threshold and key must never be retuned for final performance.

freeze_breaking_fixes.defect: The load head shared the four REQUEST tiers with run/peak, but the paper's loading cost is T_load(d, g), a function of the deployment and the device, so a request feature could move the predicted load.
freeze_breaking_fixes.fix: the load head has its own key (model_id, lane) with a train-wide default, and is excluded from the request-conditioned spread the non-degeneracy gate measures.
freeze_breaking_fixes.verification: latency_aware_fidelity 18, scheduler 13, fusion 14 green; changing only the action moves run while load stays fixed.

freeze_breaking_fixes.defect: Eq (5) prefetch ran at the TOP of the simulator loop, before ready dispatch, and its eligibility filter only checked gpu.active_node / prefetch_pending, so a prefetch could seize a device that ready work needed and push gpu.busy_until past now.
freeze_breaking_fixes.fix: prefetch is decided AFTER ready dispatch and only on devices still idle once every runnable unit has been placed, so preparing near-ready work cannot delay ready work.
freeze_breaking_fixes.verification: tests/test_latency_aware_scheduler.py test_prefetch_does_not_delay_ready_work fails on the old ordering (job starts at 250 ms) and passes on the fix (150 ms).

information_contract.note: The paper observes only the RESOLVED logical window L_t (a branch enters only after its control result resolves). The Constructor and the near-ready window read runtime-resolved nodes only; reading the realized template's unexecuted suffix would be a structure leak.
information_contract.supersedes: logical_graph_assumed_known (too strong; corrected 2026-09-26 per paper Sec 3.2)
